description: A rare and deadly disease in people and nonhuman primates.
causes: Ebola virus, spread through direct contact with infected blood or body fluids.
prevention: Avoid contact with infected individuals and animals, and practice good hygiene.
treatment_action: Supportive care (fluids, electrolytes) and experimental treatments.
complications: Organ failure, severe bleeding, and death.

description: A condition that makes your skin red and itchy.
causes: Gene variation, environmental triggers, and immune system overactivity.
prevention: Moisturize skin, avoid triggers, and use mild soaps.
treatment_action: Moisturizers, corticosteroid creams, and light therapy.
complications: Skin infections, asthma, and hay fever.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A lung condition that causes shortness of breath due to damage to the air sacs (alveoli).
causes: Smoking and long-term exposure to airborne irritants.
prevention: Don't smoke and avoid secondhand smoke.
treatment_action: Inhalers, oxygen therapy, and pulmonary rehabilitation.
complications: Collapsed lung (pneumothorax), heart problems, and large holes in the lungs (bullae).
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A disorder in which tissue similar to the tissue that normally lines the inside of your uterus grows outside your uterus.
causes: Retrograde menstruation, cellular transformation, and immune system disorders.
symptoms: Pain with bowel movements or urination
prevention: No known way to prevent, but hormonal birth control can manage symptoms.
treatment_action: Pain medications, hormone therapy, and surgery.
complications: Infertility and increased risk of ovarian cancer.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A neurological disorder in which brain activity becomes abnormal, causing seizures.
causes: Genetics, head trauma, brain conditions, and infectious diseases.
prevention: Prevent head injuries and treat infections promptly.
treatment_action: Anti-seizure medications, surgery, or dietary therapy.
complications: Falls, drowning, car accidents, and status epilepticus.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

prevention: Keep skin clean and treat cuts promptly.

description: Cancer that occurs in the esophagus — a long, hollow tube that runs from your throat to your stomach.
causes: Smoking, alcohol use, chronic acid reflux, and obesity.
prevention: Quit smoking, limit alcohol, and manage acid reflux.
treatment_action: Surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and targeted therapy.
complications: Obstruction of the esophagus, pain, and bleeding.
